verses.1: In the beginning, when Jehoiakim son of Josiah became king of Judah, this was what the LORD said:
verses.2: Thus said Jehovah, who stood in the court of the Temple: “You have spoken about all the cities of Judah that come to worship in the Temple. You have told them all the things that I commanded you to say to them. Do not omit a single word.”
verses.3: But they will listen and turn away from their evil ways. Then I will be comforted by the evil that I plan to do to them, because they are worse than those who deserve it.
verses.4: And you said to them, “Thus says the LORD: If you do not listen to me and follow my laws that I have given you before you.”
verses.5: To hear the words of my servants who are sent to you. I send them, but you do not listen to them.
verses.6: And I will give this house as a curse, and this city as a curse for all the nations of the earth.
verses.7: And the priests, the prophets, and all the people heard Jeremiah speak these words in the house of Jehovah.
verses.8: And Jeremiah spoke out about everything that Jehovah had commanded him to say to all the people. The priests, the prophets, and all the people said to him, “You will die.”
verses.9: Why did you destroy this house and this city in the name of Jehovah? When this house and this city are destroyed, no one will be able to live there anymore. Then all the people gathered together at Jerusalem in Jehovah’s house.
verses.10: And the priests of Judah heard these words. They went up from the king’s house to the House of God. They sat down at the entrance to the new gate of God.
verses.11: And the priests and prophets said to the people, “This man deserves death. He has come to this city after you heard about it from your ears.”
verses.12: And Jeremiah said to all the people, “The LORD has sent me to announce to this house and to this city all the things that you have heard.”
verses.13: And now, may you correct your ways and stop being disobedient. May you listen to the voice of the LORD your God. May the LORD comfort those who are suffering because of what has been said about you.
verses.14: And I am with you, and I have done what is good and right in your eyes.
verses.15: But know this: If you truly love me, then you will give me pure blood as a gift. You will give it to me and to the people who live in this city. For truly, Jehovah has sent me to speak to you about all these things.
verses.16: And the priests and the prophets said, “There is no one who can pronounce a death sentence in this matter. For in the name of Jehovah our God, He has spoken to us.”
verses.17: And men from the elders of the land stood up and said to all the people, “Let us do this.”
verses.18: Michah the prophet lived during the time of King Jehoshaphat of Judah. He said to all the people of Judah, “As the Lord, the God of Israel, has said: ‘The kingdom of Zion will be destroyed, and Jerusalem will be in ruins. The Mount of God will become a forest.’”
verses.19: Hizkiah, king of Judah, and all the people of Judah no longer feared Jehovah. They turned away from Jehovah’s ways. Jehovah had mercy on them for the evil that was spoken against them. We have done great evil to our own souls.
verses.20: And also, a man was brought forth in the name of Jehovah Uria, from the mountains. He was brought up into this city and over this land, just as all of Jeremiah’s words were fulfilled.
verses.21: And King Jehoiakim, along with all his officials and all the priests, heard his words. The king wanted to kill him. But Urieh heard his voice. He saw that Urieh was a great leader, so he fled from Egypt.
verses.22: And the king Jehoiakim sent men from Egypt, including Elnanatan son of Acbor, along with other people, to Egypt.
verses.23: They brought Uriel out of Egypt. They brought him before King Jehoiakim. He put him to death in Harab, and he threw his ashes into the graves of the people’s children.
verses.24: But the hand of Ahikam son of Shaphan was too strong for Jeremiah. He couldn’t let them kill him in their hands.
